title: Calibrate a step-audit statevector simulator on Chen 2024 Step 9 before it audits any live claim
claim: A small exact statevector simulator of a claimed quantum lattice step, run at toy modulus and dimension, detects the known Step-9 failure of Chen 2024 (KN-LIT-52ce4c): the simulated output distribution of the windowed-QFT stage deviates from the distribution the paper's step asserts by total variation >= 0.2 at n=2..4. The same simulator run on a corrected textbook step (Regev's Fourier sampling on an exact coset state) reproduces the asserted distribution within TV <= 0.02. Only a simulator that passes both is admitted as the instrument for auditing Simon 2026 or Luo 2026.
mechanism: Step audits in this goal are otherwise prose reviews. A load-bearing quantum step usually asserts that some register, after a transform and a measurement, has a stated distribution; at toy sizes that distribution is exactly computable by dense linear algebra. A retracted claim with a publicly named failing step is the only available positive control: if the simulator cannot see a bug that is known to exist, its silence on another claim means nothing. A correct textbook step is the negative control showing the simulator does not manufacture discrepancies from discretisation.
tracked_object: Total variation distance between the simulated post-measurement distribution of the audited register and the distribution asserted by the audited step, per (n, q, window width).

title: Signed-C cancellation ratio in Simon 2026 Lemma 3, measured by exact simulation at reduced group size
claim: In Simon's DCP erasure step (KN-LIT-e204ab), the amplitude gap between h*=0 and h*=1 is a signed sum over z* of count differences times C_{z*}. At reduced bit-length n in {6,8,10} and reduced group exponent c in {1,2,3}, the cancellation ratio R = |sum_z C_z| / sum_z |C_z| is at most 0.1 on average over secrets, so the bound in Lemma 3 that treats C as well-behaved fails at these sizes, and the measured bias of h* toward d_n is below 0.05.
mechanism: KN-LIT-e204ab names the signed-C cancellation as the entire game and KN-LIT-3b271a reports a no-go for the algorithm. Both are text-level. The quantity is classically computable at small n: the B-side contributions C depend only on the low bits of z* and are explicit sums of roots of unity over measured y values, so one can enumerate them exactly. A measured R near 1 would support Lemma 3's intent; R near 0 with negligible bias would corroborate the no-go numerically and pin which step fails.
tracked_object: Per-instance cancellation ratio R and the exact probability that the Hadamard measurement of h* returns d_n, as functions of (n, c, number of groups).

title: Adaptive versus fixed partition in Simon's erasure step: does the independence condition named by Guo-Yang carry the bias?
claim: Guo and Yang (KN-LIT-a2a423) isolate an unproved condition: the A/B partition must be fixed independently of the measured string, while the algorithm chooses it from the measurement. At toy size the h* bias toward d_n differs by at least 0.1 between a partition fixed in advance (oracle-free but unrealisable) and the adaptive partition the algorithm actually uses. If the bias exists only under the fixed partition, the gap is exactly the unproved condition.
mechanism: The Lemma 2 cancellation argument holds for any fixed partition. Selecting A as the all-zero-Hadamard groups correlates A with the measured b' values, which can reweight the z* branches unequally. Exact enumeration lets both partitions be computed on identical randomness, isolating the effect of adaptivity alone.
tracked_object: Difference in exact Pr[h* = d_n] between adaptive (as specified) and fixed-in-advance partitions on identical secrets and measurement outcomes.

positive: fixed partition with Regev oracle erasure (bias near 1/2)
A/A: adaptive arm under two seed blocks

falsification_conditions: Adaptive and fixed biases agree within 0.03 at all sizes
confounders: Fixed partition may change post-selection probability, confounding bias with acceptance rate
interpretation_limits: Scale limit: toy n<=10; identifies which condition carries the effect at small size, no asymptotic statement

title: Luo Part III Voronoi claim at small 2-power conductors: is the CVP target from a short ring element inside the origin's Voronoi cell?

title: Structure-blindness test for quantum enumeration: is the Montanaro tree size on ring and module bases the same as on plain LWE?
claim: The quantum-frontier schema classifies rows as structure-blind or structure-dependent, but for quantum enumeration (KN-LIT-3072) the cost is a function of the classical enumeration tree size T (roughly sqrt(T) quantum steps). title: Measure the Grover search-space sizes a quantum sieve would actually face: instrumented G6K bucket/filter sizes priced with QRAM
claim: KN-LIT-122 prices quantum near-neighbour search from modelled bucket sizes. Instrumenting G6K's bucketed sieve at dims 50-90 on lattices shaped like ML-KEM and ML-DSA key recovery, the measured mean bucket size deviates from the model's prediction by at least 15% at some dimension, and when Grover cost is computed from measured sizes with QRAM priced at 0, 0.1 and 1 gate-equivalents per query, the quantum/classical cost ratio at dim 90 differs from the model's by at least 2 bits at price 1.
mechanism: Quantum sieve speedup lives in searching buckets with Grover; its value depends on bucket size distributions (Grover cost sqrt(size), but variance matters since sum of sqrt is not sqrt of mean) and on QRAM loads. Measured distributions replace model means, and both schemes share the same instrument. 472aa2 asserts QRAM inputs are hidden; this measures the input distribution.

title: A shared A/A noise-floor registry for lattice-reduction measurements: minimum detectable effect per instrument, shape and dimension
claim: Across BKZ (fpylll) and sieving (G6K) measurements on ML-KEM- and ML-DSA-shaped lattices, run-to-run variability from basis randomisation, instance sampling and thread scheduling sets a minimum detectable effect (MDE at 80% power) of at least 0.3 bits for log-cost quantities at dims 60-100. Several calibration proposals in this RQ target effects at or below that size, so without the registry their outcomes cannot be distinguished from noise.

title: Memory-capped sieving: success and cost when G6K's database is held below the 2^{0.2075n} list size, on both schemes' lattices
claim: Holding G6K's database size factor below 1 (0.5, 0.7, 0.85 of default) at dims 60-90 on ML-KEM- and ML-DSA-shaped lattices, the saturation success probability falls below 0.5 at a factor of about 0.7, and the cost-memory tradeoff exponent (d log time / d log memory) near the floor is at least -2, so memory-charged cost with an area-time price cannot be lowered by more than 2 bits by shrinking memory.
mechanism: Memory-charged cost models (area x time) reward smaller memory only if time does not explode. The tradeoff near the minimal list size is unmeasured; 7bc28c prices access pattern, fc6361 counts saturation balls at full size, 70e41d moves the crossover with memory price. This measures the time penalty of capping memory directly, one instrument for both schemes.
